title: Pullback of modules commutes with tensor products, compatibly with sections
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with pullback $f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor product $\otimes$ of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an open $V\subseteq Y$ and a section $u\in\mathcal H(V)$ of an $\mathcal O_Y$-module write $f^*u\in(f^*\mathcal H)(f^{-1}V)$ for its image under the unit $\mathcal H\to f_*f^*\mathcal H$ of $f^*\dashv f_*$, and for sections $s,t$ over one open write $s\otimes t$ for the image of $s\otimes t$ in the tensor product sheaf. Then there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$f^*(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal G)\;\cong\;f^*\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f^*\mathcal G,$$
natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$, which sends $f^*(s\otimes t)$ to $f^*s\otimes f^*t$ for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.16.4 (Tag 01CD, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback; proof omitted in the source). A proof: the map is adjoint to the $\mathcal O_Y$-bilinear map $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to f_*(f^*\mathcal F\otimes f^*\mathcal G)$, $(s,t)\mapsto f^*s\otimes f^*t$, and is an isomorphism on stalks by Sheaves Tag 0098 and Modules Tag 01CB together with $(A\otimes_RB)\otimes_RS\cong(A\otimes_RS)\otimes_S(B\otimes_RS)$; isomorphisms are detected on stalks (Modules Tag 01AG). Lean (slopmaster2, sorry_here, existence only): AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_pullback_tensorObj_iso, WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/ProjectionFormula.lean lines 62-68

proof.text: *(1) Construction of the map.* Write $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$ for the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], so $f^*u=\eta(u)$ for a section $u$, and put $\mathcal T=f^*\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f^*\mathcal G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an open $V\subseteq Y$ define $\beta_V:\mathcal F(V)\times\mathcal G(V)\to(f_*\mathcal T)(V)=\mathcal T(f^{-1}V)$ by $\beta_V(s,t)=f^*s\otimes f^*t$. It is $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-bilinear for the $\mathcal O_Y$-module structure of $f_*\mathcal T$ (in which $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acts through $f^\sharp(a)\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$): $\eta_{\mathcal F}$ is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear, so $f^*(as)=f^\sharp(a)f^*s$, and $\otimes$ is $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$-bilinear on sections; additivity is the same. It commutes with restriction to $V'\subseteq V$, since $\eta$ is a morphism of sheaves and the map $u\otimes w\mapsto u\otimes w$ into $\mathcal T$ commutes with restrictions. Hence the maps $\beta_V$ induce $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear maps $\mathcal F(V)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y(V)}\mathcal G(V)\to(f_*\mathcal T)(V)$ forming a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal G\to f_*\mathcal T$. The target is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules (the pushforward of a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, [def-pc-module-pullback]), so by the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it factors uniquely through $\mathcal F\otimes_{p}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal G$: there is a unique $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $\beta:\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal G\to f_*\mathcal T$ with $\beta(s\otimes t)=f^*s\otimes f^*t$ (this is Stacks' characterization $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G,\mathcal H)=\operatorname{Bilin}(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G,\mathcal H)$, Modules Section 17.16). Let $\alpha=\alpha_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:f^*(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal G)\to\mathcal T$ be the morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules adjoint to $\beta$ under $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], i.e. the unique one with $f_*(\alpha)\circ\eta_{\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G}=\beta$.

source.place: Modules, Section 17.16 (Tag 01CA, label section-tensor-product: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G,\mathcal H)=\operatorname{Bilin}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G,\mathcal H)$); compare Modules on Sites, Lemma Tag 03EL (sites-modules lemma-tensor-product-pullback), whose proof goes through the same adjunction and bilinear maps

proof.text: *(2) The formula on sections.* For $V\subseteq Y$ open, $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$: $\alpha(f^*(s\otimes t))=\alpha(\eta(s\otimes t))=(f_*(\alpha)\circ\eta)(s\otimes t)=\beta(s\otimes t)=f^*s\otimes f^*t$, the sections of $f_*$ over $V$ being those over $f^{-1}V$ and $f_*(\alpha)_V=\alpha_{f^{-1}V}$. This is the defining identity of $\alpha$ from step (1) evaluated on a section.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.16.4 (Tag 01CD, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback; proof omitted in the source)

proof.text: The map constructed in steps (1)–(2) satisfies the section formula. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor-iso-criterion] to conclude that it is an isomorphism, and form the resulting isomorphism using asIso.

*(6) Naturality.* Let $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $v:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be $\mathcal O_Y$-linear, with $u\otimes v$ the induced map of tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (sheafification of $s\otimes t\mapsto u(s)\otimes v(t)$, so $(u\otimes v)(s\otimes t)=u(s)\otimes v(t)$ on sections). The two $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\alpha_{\mathcal F',\mathcal G'}\circ f^*(u\otimes v)$ and $(f^*u\otimes f^*v)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}$ from $f^*(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)$ to $f^*\mathcal F'\otimes f^*\mathcal G'$ are equal: by the adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback] it suffices that their adjoints $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G\to f_*(f^*\mathcal F'\otimes f^*\mathcal G')$ (composition with $\eta_{\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G}$, after $f_*$) agree, and by the uniqueness in the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it suffices that they agree on the sections $s\otimes t$, which generate the presheaf tensor product over $\mathcal O_Y(V)$. Using the naturality of the unit, $f^*(w)(f^*z)=f^*(w(z))$ for a morphism $w$ and a section $z$, and step (2): the first sends $s\otimes t$ to $\alpha(f^*(u(s)\otimes v(t)))=f^*(u(s))\otimes f^*(v(t))$; the second sends it to $(f^*u\otimes f^*v)(f^*s\otimes f^*t)=f^*(u(s))\otimes f^*(v(t))$. Hence $\alpha$ is natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.
